notes.key_messages: To gain high marks for a coursework assignment a candidate should: ● ensure the assignment title is a question which requires investigation ● ensure the question is an analytical question rather than a descriptive question ● use both primary and secondary research to gather information relevant to the question and then analyse this information ● end with a conclusion which answers the question posed in the title and is based on the information gathered.
notes.general_comments: Most Centres that submitted coursework were experienced in its delivery and have submitted coursework over several years. The assignment titles used by candidates had usually been used successfully in previous years and most assignments included a feasibility study, a motivation analysis or an analysis of the marketing mix used by a business. Assessment criteria Questionnaires were, for the majority of candidates, the most popular form of gathering primary research. Sources of information selected by some candidates included visits to businesses, interviews (with business people and the general public), the Internet and information such as advertisements, maps and photographs. Some candidates discussed their approach to the research; who, when, why and how it was carried out. This was helpful, often contributing to them gaining higher marks for Assessment Objective 2. In addition textbooks were also used to provide an explanation of the business concepts and terminology applied to research findings. The majority of assignment titles were analytical, so encouraging a wide range of research. A minority of titles were descriptive such as ‘What are the wants and needs of customers of ..... business?’ These titles could still encourage a candidate to undertake a wide range of research. but the candidate’s analysis and evaluation of this information was likely to be lacking in detail and consequently could result in lower marks than might have been gained had a different title been set. Better candidates posed analytical questions (e.g. Is the marketing mix of …………successful?), which they answered in the conclusion, so gaining higher marks for Assessment Objective 4. Candidates made very effective use of IT in presenting their coursework. The majority of candidates presented their findings in a logical manner with a clear title, an outline of the problem/question set, the research findings with analysis of the data and a conclusion that answered the question posed in the title. Application of the Assessment Criteria The assessment criteria were accurately applied by most Centres - this was a reflection of the experience of the teachers in assessing coursework. Where descriptive titles had been chosen by candidates or too narrow a range of information had been gathered -which had then limited the analysis and evaluation in the assignment - then the marks awarded by teachers were not usually generous but were an accurate assessment of the work. Where candidates scored lower marks, it was usually due to the lack of detailed analysis of the data gathered or lack of a justified conclusion based on the evidence gathered. Assignment Titles Most candidates had a clearly stated question at the beginning of their assignment; these were questions that encouraged analysis and evaluation of the data collected and so resulted in high marks being awarded. The most popular topic was a feasibility study, which was phrased slightly differently by different candidates, for example: ‘Would it be profitable to set up a ….... in ……….(my neighbourhood)?’ Other titles were: ‘What motivation strategies can …..adopt in order to reduce their labour turnover?’ ‘How can a small business like ………….attract more clients?’ ‘Can the marketing mix of ……. be improved?’ ‘Is the marketing mix of ……….. more successful than …….?’ All the administration procedures were adhered to and samples of coursework were sent by the deadline. All of this made the moderation process proceed smoothly – Centres are to be thanked for their efficiency.
